props.gloss_en: bowls one ate from at night may be rinsed to eat from in the morning; morning ones for noon; noon ones for the afternoon
from the afternoon onward he no longer rinses them
but cups, ladles and flasks he rinses all day long
because there is no fixed time for drinking
whoever keeps three meals on Shabbat is saved from three calamities: the birth-pangs of the Messiah, the judgment of Gehinnom, and the war of Gog and Magog
whoever delights in Shabbat is given an inheritance without boundaries

as it says 'then you shall delight in the Lord ... and I will feed you the inheritance of Jacob your father' (Is 58:14) -- not like Abraham ('walk the land in its length', Gen 13:17), nor like Isaac ('to you and your seed I will give all these lands', Gen 26:3), but like Jacob ('you shall spread out west, east, north and south', Gen 28:14)
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: [one who delights in Shabbat] is saved from subjugation to the kingdoms
whoever delights in Shabbat is given his heart's desires

as it says 'delight in the Lord and He will give you your heart's desires' (Ps 37:4); this delight I do not know what it is -- when it says 'and you shall call Shabbat a delight' (Is 58:13), say: this is the delight of Shabbat
with what does one delight it? with a dish of beets, large fish and heads of garlic
even a small thing, if he made it in honour of Shabbat, is oneg
what is it [the small thing]? Rav Papa: a dish of small fish fried in flour (כסא דהרסנא)
whoever keeps Shabbat according to its law, even if he worships idols like the generation of Enosh, is forgiven
as it says 'happy is the man [enosh] who does this ... who keeps Shabbat from desecrating it' (Is 56:2) -- read not 'from desecrating it' (מחללו) but 'he is forgiven' (מחול לו)
had Israel kept the first Shabbat, no nation or tongue would have ruled over them
were Israel to keep two Shabbatot according to their law, they would be redeemed at once
R' Yosei: may my portion be among those who eat three meals on Shabbat
R' Yosei: may my portion be among those who complete Hallel every day
the master: one who reads Hallel every day is a blasphemer and a reviler
R' Yosei: may my portion be among those who pray with the reddening of the sun
it is a mitzva to pray with the reddening of the sun
R' Zeira: what is the verse? 'they shall fear You with the sun and before the moon, throughout all generations' (Ps 72:5)
R' Yosei: may my portion be among those who die of intestinal illness
as the master said: most of the righteous die of intestinal illness
R' Yosei: may my portion be among those who die on the way to a mitzva
R' Yosei: may my portion be among those who bring in Shabbat in Tiberias and take it out in Tzippori
R' Yosei: may my portion be among those who seat [the students in] the study hall, not among those who make [them] stand
R' Yosei: may my portion be among the collectors of charity, not among its distributors
R' Yosei: may my portion be with one who is suspected [of a fault] and it is not in him
Rav Papa: they suspected me and it was not in me
R' Yosei: I had relations five times and planted five cedars in Israel -- R' Yishmael, R' Elazar, R' Chalafta, R' Avtilas and R' Menachem, sons of R' Yosei
but there is Vardimas [a sixth son]!
Vardimas is Menachem; why is he called Vardimas? because his face resembles a rose
is that to say R' Yosei did not fulfil the mitzva of conjugal duty?
rather say: I had relations five times [which bore children] and repeated [them]
R' Yosei: never did I call my wife 'my wife' or my ox 'my ox', but my wife 'my home' and my ox 'my field'
R' Yosei: never did I look at my circumcision
they said to Rabbi: why do they call you 'our holy rabbi'? he said: never did I look at my circumcision
in Rabbi there was another thing: he never put his hand beneath his belt
R' Yosei: never did the beams of my house see the seams of my shirt
R' Yosei: never did I transgress the words of my colleagues; I know I am not a priest, yet if my colleagues tell me 'go up to the platform', I go up
R' Yosei: never did I say a thing and go back on it
Rav Nachman: may [reward] come to me, for I kept three meals on Shabbat
Rav Yehuda: may [reward] come to me, for I kept concentration in prayer
Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua: may [reward] come to me, for I never walked four cubits bareheaded
Rav Sheshet: may [reward] come to me, for I kept the mitzva of tefillin
Rav Nachman: may [reward] come to me, for I kept the mitzva of tzitzit
Rav Yosef to Rav Yosef son of Rabba: your father -- in what was he most careful?
in tzitzit: one day he was climbing a ladder, a thread snapped, and he did not come down until he had put it back
Abaye: may [reward] come to me, for when I see a young scholar who has finished his tractate, I make a feast for the rabbis
Rava: may [reward] come to me, for when a young scholar comes before me for judgment, I do not lay my head on the pillow until I have sought out his merit
Mar bar Rav Ashi: I disqualify myself from judging a young scholar
why? because he is as dear to me as myself, and a person does not see fault in himself
R' Chanina would wrap himself and stand at dusk on Shabbat eve and say: come, let us go out to greet Shabbat the queen
R' Yannai would put on fine garments, wrap himself and say: come, bride; come, bride
Rabba bar Rav Huna visited Rabba bar Rav Nachman; they served him three se'ahs of cakes; he said: did you know I was coming?
they said to him: are you more important to us than it [Shabbat]?
R' Abba would buy meat for thirteen istira from thirteen butchers and hand it over at the door, saying: hurry, hurry
R' Abbahu would sit on an ivory stool and fan the fire
Rav Anan would wear a work smock
garments in which one cooked a pot for his master -- let him not pour a cup for his master in them
Rav Safra would singe the [animal's] head
Rava would salt the shibuta fish
Rav Huna would light the lamps
Rav Papa would twist the wicks
Rav Chisda would chop beets
Rabba and Rav Yosef would split wood
R' Zeira would kindle kindling
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak would carry [loads] in and carry out
he said: if R' Ami and R' Assi came to me, would I not carry before them?
R' Ami and R' Assi would carry in and carry out, saying: if R' Yochanan visited us, would we not carry before him?
the Chaldeans to the rich gentile: all your property -- Yosef who honours Shabbat will consume it
Yosef who honours Shabbat, who habitually bought [for Shabbat], bought the fish on Shabbat eve, cut it open, found the pearl, and sold it for thirteen attics of gold dinars
the old man: whoever borrows for Shabbat, Shabbat repays him
Rabbi to R' Yishmael son of R' Yosei: the rich of Eretz Yisrael -- in what do they merit [it]?
because they tithe
as it says 'you shall surely tithe' (Deut 14:22) -- tithe so that you will become rich
those of Babylonia? because they honour the Torah
and those of other lands? because they honour Shabbat
R' Chiyya bar Abba: I was once a guest of a householder in Laodicea; they brought before him a golden table carried by sixteen men ... I said to him: my son, by what did you merit this?
the householder: I was a butcher, and of every fine animal I said: this one shall be for Shabbat
R' Chiyya bar Abba: happy are you that you merited, and blessed is the Omnipresent who made you merit this
the Emperor to R' Yehoshua ben Chananya: why does the Shabbat dish smell so fragrant?
we have one spice called Shabbat, which we put into it and its smell spreads
the Emperor: give us some of it
for whoever keeps Shabbat it works; for whoever does not keep Shabbat it does not work

the Exilarch asks Rav Hamnuna the meaning of 'and the holy one of the Lord honoured' (Is 58:13); he answers: this is Yom Kippur, which has neither eating nor drinking -- the Torah said: honour it with clean clothing
'and you shall honour it' (Is 58:13) -- Rav: [by eating the Shabbat meal] earlier
Shmuel: later
the sons of Rav Papa bar Abba to Rav Papa: for us, who have meat and wine every day -- how shall we distinguish it?
Rav Papa: if you usually eat early, make it later; if you usually eat late, make it earlier
Rav Sheshet in summer would seat the rabbis where the sun reached, in winter where the shade reached, so that they would get up quickly
R' Zeira would seek out pairs of rabbis [studying on Shabbat eve] and say to them: I beg of you, do not desecrate it
even an individual praying on Shabbat eve must say Vayechulu
Rav Hamnuna: whoever prays on Shabbat eve and says Vayechulu, Scripture considers him as if he became a partner with the Holy One in the work of creation
as it says 'and they were finished' (Gen 2:1) -- read not 'they were finished' (ויכולו) but 'they finished' (ויכלו)
R' Elazar: from where [do we know] that speech is like action?
as it says 'by the word of the Lord the heavens were made' (Ps 33:6)

whoever prays on Shabbat eve and says Vayechulu, the two ministering angels who accompany a person place their hands on his head and say to him: 'your iniquity is removed and your sin atoned' (Is 6:7)

two ministering angels accompany a person on Shabbat eve from the synagogue home, one good and one evil; if he finds a lamp lit, a table set and his bed made, the good angel says 'may it be so next Shabbat' and the evil one answers Amen against its will; if not, the evil angel says it and the good one answers Amen against its will
R' Elazar: a person should always set his table on Shabbat eve, even if he needs only an olive's bulk
R' Chanina: a person should always set his table on Motzaei Shabbat, even if he needs only an olive's bulk
hot water on Motzaei Shabbat is a remedy; warm bread on Motzaei Shabbat is a remedy
for R' Abbahu they would prepare a third-grown calf at the departure of Shabbat, and he would eat its kidney
Avimi to his father: why waste so much? let us leave a kidney from Shabbat eve
they left it [the calf], and a lion came and ate it
whoever answers 'Amen, may His great name be blessed' with all his strength, his decree is torn up
as it says 'when retribution was annulled in Israel, when the people offered themselves, bless the Lord' (Jud 5:2)
why 'when retribution was annulled'? because of 'bless the Lord'
even if he has a trace of idolatry, he is forgiven
whoever answers Amen with all his strength, the gates of the Garden of Eden are opened for him
as it says 'open the gates, that the righteous nation that keeps faithfulness may enter' (Is 26:2) -- read not 'that keeps faithfulness' (שומר אמונים) but 'that says amen' (שאומרים אמן)
what is 'amen'? R' Chanina: 'God, faithful King'
fire is found only in a place where there is desecration of Shabbat

as it says 'but if you will not listen to Me to sanctify the Shabbat day and not to carry a burden ... then I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem, and it shall not be quenched' (Jer 17:27)
what is 'and it shall not be quenched'? Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: at a time when people are not available to put it out
Abaye: Jerusalem was destroyed only because they desecrated Shabbat in it, as it says 'and they hid their eyes from My Shabbatot, and I was profaned among them' (Ezek 22:26)
'and they hid their eyes from My Shabbatot, and I was profaned among them' (Ezek 22:26)
R' Abbahu: Jerusalem was destroyed only because they neglected the morning and evening Shema

as it says 'woe to those who rise early to pursue strong drink' (Is 5:11), and 'the harp and the lute ... and wine are their feasts, and they regard not the work of the Lord' (Is 5:12), and 'therefore My people go into exile for lack of knowledge' (Is 5:13)
Rav Hamnuna: Jerusalem was destroyed only because they neglected the schoolchildren in it
as it says 'pour it out upon the children in the street' (Jer 6:11)
why 'pour out'? because the children are in the street
Ulla: Jerusalem was destroyed only because they had no shame before one another, as it says 'they were ashamed because they committed abomination; nay, they are not at all ashamed' (Jer 6:15)
'they were ashamed ... nay, they are not at all ashamed' (Jer 6:15)
R' Yitzchak: Jerusalem was destroyed only because small and great were made equal
R' Chanina: Jerusalem was destroyed only because they did not rebuke one another

as it says 'her princes are like harts that find no pasture' (Lam 1:6) -- as with harts, each one's head is beside the other's tail, so Israel of that generation hid their faces in the ground and did not rebuke one another
R' Yehuda: Jerusalem was destroyed only because they despised Torah scholars in it
as it says 'but they mocked the messengers of God, despised His words and scoffed at His prophets, until the wrath of the Lord rose against His people, till there was no remedy' (II Chr 36:16)
what is 'till there was no remedy'? Rav Yehuda said Rav said: whoever despises Torah scholars has no cure for his wound
what is meant by 'touch not My anointed and do My prophets no harm' (Ps 105:15)? 'My anointed' -- schoolchildren; 'My prophets' -- Torah scholars
the world endures only for the sake of the breath of schoolchildren
Rav Papa to Abaye: what of mine and yours [our breath in study]?
Abaye: breath that has sin in it is not like breath that has no sin in it
one does not interrupt schoolchildren [from study] even for the building of the Temple
Reish Lakish to R' Yehuda Nesia: thus I have received from my fathers (and some say: from your fathers) -- any city that has no schoolchildren is destroyed
Ravina: it is placed under a ban
Rava: Jerusalem was destroyed only because men of trust ceased from it
as it says 'run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem ... if you can find a man, if there is any who does justly, who seeks faithfulness, and I will pardon her' (Jer 5:1)
Rav Ketina: even at the hour of Jerusalem's downfall, men of trust did not cease from it

as it says 'when a man takes hold of his brother in his father's house: you have a cloak, be our ruler' (Is 3:6) -- matters people cover themselves with like a cloak are in your hands; 'and this ruin under your hand' -- matters people do not grasp unless they stumble in them; 'in that day he shall swear (ישא -- an oath, as in 'you shall not take [תשא] the name'): I will not be a binder' (Is 3:7) -- I will not be of those confined in the study hall; 'and in my house is neither bread nor cloak' -- I have neither Bible, Mishna nor Gemara. He refuses office rather than claim learning he lacks
it is not difficult: here [Rav Ketina] in matters of Torah, there [Rava] in business dealings

schemas.gloss_en: מחבלו של משיח: כתיב הכא 'יום' וכתיב התם 'הנה אנכי שולח לכם את אליה הנביא לפני בוא יום' (Mal 3:23)
מדינה של גיהנם: כתיב הכא 'יום' וכתיב התם 'יום עברה היום ההוא' (Zeph 1:15)
ממלחמת גוג ומגוג: כתיב הכא 'יום' וכתיב התם 'ביום בא גוג' (Ezek 38:18)
כתיב הכא 'והרכבתיך על במתי ארץ' (Is 58:14) וכתיב התם 'ואתה על במותימו תדרך' (Deut 33:29) -- the one who delights in Shabbat treads on the kingdoms' high places
שנאמר 'ויהי ביום השביעי יצאו מן העם ללקוט' (Ex 16:27) וכתיב בתריה 'ויבא עמלק' (Ex 17:8) -- Rav's derivation, as Rav Yehuda transmits it
שנאמר 'כה אמר ה' לסריסים אשר ישמרו את שבתותי' (Is 56:4) וכתיב בתריה 'והביאותים אל הר קדשי' (Is 56:7) -- RShbY's derivation, as R' Yochanan transmits it; 'Shabbatot' read as two
כתיב הכא 'בפרוע פרעות' (Jud 5:2) וכתיב התם 'כי פרוע הוא' (Ex 32:25, the golden calf) -- even one with a trace of idolatry is forgiven
שנאמר 'והיה כעם ככהן' (Is 24:2) וכתיב בתריה 'הבוק תבוק הארץ' (Is 24:3)

supports.gloss_en: שנאמר ... והאכלתיך נחלת יעקב אביך -- R' Yosei's derivation, as R' Yochanan transmits it
שנאמר והתענג על ה' ויתן לך משאלות לבך ... הוי אומר זה עונג שבת -- Rav's derivation
שנאמר אשרי אנוש ... מחללו -- אל תקרי מחללו אלא מחול לו
Rav Papa: לדידי חשדן ולא הוה בי -- his own experience set beside R' Yosei's wish; the text marks no further relation
אמר רבי זירא, מאי קרא: ייראוך עם שמש -- R' Zeira supplies the verse for R' Yochanan's dictum
דאמר מר: רובן של צדיקים מתים בחולי מעיים -- the stam's ground for R' Yosei's wish
מאי טעמא? דחביב עלי כגופאי, ואין אדם רואה חובה לעצמו
דתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל: בגדים שבישל בהן קדירה לרבו אל ימזוג בהן כוס לרבו -- the stam's ground for Rav Anan's smock
שנאמר עשר תעשר -- עשר בשביל שתתעשר
דאמר רבי חייא בר אבא: the householder of Laodicea, whose wealth came of setting the finest animal aside for Shabbat
דאמר רב המנונא: כל המתפלל בערב שבת ואומר ויכולו ... כאילו נעשה שותף -- the stam's ground for the individual's obligation
שנאמר ויכולו -- אל תקרי ויכולו אלא ויכלו
שנאמר בדבר ה' שמים נעשו
שנאמר בפרוע פרעות בישראל ... ברכו ה'
שנאמר פתחו שערים ... שומר אמונים -- אל תיקרי שומר אמונים אלא שאומרים אמן
שנאמר ... והצתי אש בשעריה ... ולא תכבה -- Rav's derivation, as Rav Yehuda b. Rav Shmuel transmits it
שנאמר ומשבתותי העלימו עיניהם ואחל בתוכם
שנאמר הוי משכימי בבקר ... וכתיב ... וכתיב לכן גלה עמי מבלי דעת
שנאמר שפוך על עולל בחוץ
שנאמר הובישו כי תועבה עשו גם בוש לא יבושו
שנאמר היו שריה כאילים לא מצאו מרעה -- מה איל זה ... אף ישראל -- R' Chanina's derivation, as transmitted
שנאמר ויהיו מלעיבים במלאכי האלהים ... עד לאין מרפא
שנאמר שוטטו בחוצות ירושלים ... אם יש איש עושה משפט מבקש אמונה
שנאמר כי יתפש איש באחיו ... לא אהיה חבש ... ובביתי אין לחם ואין שמלה -- the man refuses office rather than claim learning he lacks

deflected_by.gloss_en: ומממאי? דילמא שאני התם, דאי אמר להו גמירנא, אמרו ליה: אימא לן -- perhaps he refuses only because, had he claimed learning, they would say 'tell us' and expose him; that is no proof of trustworthiness

refuted_by.gloss_en: הוה ליה למימר גמר ושכח, מאי לא אהיה חובש? כלל! -- he could have said 'I learned and forgot'; his oath 'I will not be a binder' at all shows honesty

objections.gloss_en: איני?! והאמר מר: הקורא הלל בכל יום הרי זה מחרף ומגדף -- kind svara under protest: the schema has no ObjectionKind for an amoraic-memra contradiction

answered_by.gloss_en: כי קאמרינן -- בפסוקי דזמרא: R' Yosei meant the verses of praise, not Hallel

objections.gloss_en: והאיכא ורדימס -- but R' Yosei had a son Vardimas, a sixth

answered_by.gloss_en: Vardimas is Menachem, named for his rose-like face (= p_vardimas_hu_menachem)

objections.gloss_en: למימרא דרבי יוסי מצות עונה לא קיים -- read literally, R' Yosei had relations only five times

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא אימא: חמש בעילות בעלתי ושניתי -- the wording is emended (= p_beilot_veshaniti)

objections.gloss_en: איני? והאמרו ליה לרבי: מאי טעמא קרו לך רבינו הקדוש? אמר להו: מימי לא נסתכלתי במילה שלי -- the trait was Rabbi's distinction

answered_by.gloss_en: ברבי מילתא אחריתי הוה ביה -- Rabbi had a further trait: he never put his hand beneath his belt (= p_rabbi_avneto)

objections.gloss_en: איני?! והאמר רב קטינא: אפילו בשעת כשלונה של ירושלים לא פסקו ממנה אנשי אמנה -- kind svara under protest (amoraic-memra contradiction)

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: כאן בדברי תורה, כאן במשא ומתן -- men of trust in Torah remained; in business dealings they ceased (= p_kan_bedivrei_torah)
